title: When Did Oklahoma Hire Brent Venables as Head Coach?
question: When did Oklahoma hire Brent Venables, and what was his background?
answer: Oklahoma hired Brent Venables as head coach on Dec. 5, 2021, to replace Lincoln Riley. A Sooner assistant from 1999 to 2011, he came from Clemson, where he had been defensive coordinator for 10 seasons, and it was his first head coaching job.
summary: OU hired Brent Venables on Dec. 5, 2021, bringing home a former Sooner defensive coordinator from Clemson for his first head coaching job. Details here.
body: When Lincoln Riley left for USC in late November 2021, Oklahoma went back to a familiar name. On Sunday, Dec. 5, 2021, the school announced Brent Venables as its new head coach, the 23rd in program history.

Venables had deep Sooner roots. A former Kansas State linebacker under Bill Snyder, he came to Norman with Bob Stoops in 1999 as co-defensive coordinator and linebackers coach, and he was part of the staff that won the 2000 national championship. From 2004 to 2011 he served as associate head coach and sole defensive coordinator, giving him 13 seasons on the OU staff.

He then spent 10 seasons at Clemson as defensive coordinator, the last four also as associate head coach under Dabo Swinney. The Tigers won national titles after the 2016 and 2018 seasons, and Venables won the Broyles Award as the nation's top assistant coach in 2016. The Oklahoma job was his first as a head coach, making him the fourth straight OU head coach hired without previous head coaching experience.

His tenure has included the program's move into the SEC in 2024. In 2025 his Sooners went 10-2 in the regular season and earned the program's first College Football Playoff berth since 2019, hosting Alabama in a first-round game in Norman on Dec. 19, 2025.
